overview: The City Council and Community Development Board held a joint public hearing to review revised zoning amendments for Medford Square, focusing on height limits, historic preservation, and parking flexibility. The bodies voted to continue the public hearing to March 31, 2026, to allow for final technical adjustments before a final vote in late April.

items.title: Call to Order and Minutes
items.summary: The City Council and Community Development Board called their respective meetings to order and approved the records of the March 3, 2026, special joint meeting.

items.title: Public Hearing: Medford Square Zoning Amendments (Paper 26-023)
items.summary: Innes Land Group presented a revised draft of the Medford Square ordinance that includes new sub-district classifications (MS1-MS4), refined height limits for topography, and incentives for historic facade preservation and small business rent stability. The boards discussed extending the shared parking radius to 750 feet and creating 'daylight minimum' standards to protect natural light for existing residents; the hearing was continued to March 31, 2026.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents advocated for prioritizing commercial uses like bookstores and cafes over banks and medical offices, while others urged the removal of parking minimums to reduce housing costs and encourage a walkable downtown.

items.title: Medford Square City Hall Overlay District (Paper 26-058)
items.summary: The boards reviewed a proposal for a 'Transom' project overlay district covering three city-owned parcels, which will include a parking garage and specific waivers not applicable to the broader square. Further design presentation and a public hearing on this overlay were scheduled for the March 31 joint meeting.
